_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For salesbuildr the manifest gained: SALESBUILDR_BASE_URL. server.json gained: SALESBUILDR_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: SALESBUILDR_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The on-disk response cache is off on every client: raw Salesbuildr bodies never sit in cache files.
handfixes.why: Salesbuildr responses (companies, opportunities, quotes) have no business in cache files. c.NoCache = true in guardClient (salesbuildr_guard.go); TestGuardWrapsTheSessionTransport asserts it. README and SKILL say responses are never cached. The shared credential kit (credkit-wiring) would withhold a cache file carrying a held credential, but it does not stop ordinary response data being cached, so this stays.

handfixes.summary: No MCP tool changes Salesbuildr state: every endpoint tool is a GET marked read-only and every mirrored command is read-only or writes only the CLI's own files. The confirm gate stays installed so a mirrored command a later print adds that is neither read-only nor local previews and sends only with confirm: true.
handfixes.why: Work order: an MCP write previews and sends only with confirm: true. RequireConfirmForMirroredWrites (hand file internal/mcp/cobratree/salesbuildr_confirm.go), called from RegisterTools after RegisterAll. TestRegisteredMirroredWritesNeedConfirm fails on any registered tool that is not read-only, not on its local list and has no confirm gate; TestMCPSendsOnlyReads (black-box) checks a full MCP battery sends only GETs and the two logins. Ported to salesbuildr from the vsphere 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Ported to salesbuildr from the microsoft-graph 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Ported to salesbuildr from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (pax8/microsoft-graph lineage; one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: README and SKILL carry a Credential safety section (which host gets which credential, withheld output, 0600 store, dry run, MCP confirm) and no longer promise a five-minute response cache (the cache is off on every client).
handfixes.why: The generated docs describe the press defaults (a response cache) that the credential layer turns off; a reprint restores the false promise and drops the transcripts reasoning the work order requires. Ported to salesbuildr from the microsoft-graph 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Ported to salesbuildr from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (pax8/microsoft-graph lineage; one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: A client built under --dry-run refuses every request at its transport, so no write, mint or refresh can reach Salesbuildr whatever a command does with the client; `auth login --dry-run` sends nothing too.
handfixes.why: Defense in depth beside dry-run-never-mints: the generated preview path returns before sending, and this transport makes a missed branch fail closed. The black-box test runs writes and auth login under --dry-run from a cold start against a fake token host and API host and counts zero requests on both. Ported to salesbuildr from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (pax8/microsoft-graph lineage; one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: Every typed MCP endpoint tool that is not read-only (create or update a company or contact, delete a contact, create an order, update or cancel a subscription) returns a preview of the request and sends nothing until confirm is boolean true; the gate wraps every non-read-only, non-mirrored tool, so one a later print adds is gated too.
handfixes.why: Work order connector note: every MCP write must preview and send only with confirm: true. Press 4.34.2's in-process endpoint handlers (makeAPIHandler) send writes directly. The gate (hand file internal/mcp/salesbuildr_endpoint_confirm.go) is installed by one anchored line in the generated tools.go after every registration and before the read-only drop. The black-box test drives the real MCP server against a fake Salesbuildr: no write without confirm, the string "true" previews, and boolean true sends (control). Ported to salesbuildr from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (pax8/microsoft-graph lineage; one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: config.toml never holds a credential: save keeps base_url without its userinfo, query and fragment (baseURLWithoutCredentials) and leaves out every credential-named header and every header whose value, raw or decoded (base64, base32, hex, percent, up to three layers), repeats a configured or environment credential (headersWithoutCredentials), warning for each; the legacy scrub writes through the same filter; the write goes through cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile, a declared kit exemption. The 0600 credential store is unchanged.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 class credential-persisted-outside-the-store: `SALESBUILDR_BASE_URL='https://app.usesalesbuildr.com/api?api_key=X' auth set-token` wrote X (and a userinfo password, a held secret under any query name, a token_url query secret) into config.toml, because the generated save persists base_url and token_url as configured. Work order credential rule: nothing but the 0600 credential store holds a credential. Hand file internal/config/salesbuildr_persist.go; three anchored lines in the generated config.go (tools/apply_credential_rules.py). TestConfigFileNeverHoldsACredential failed on the generated save (seen/r1-config-file-credential-seen-failing.log). Ported to salesbuildr from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (pax8/microsoft-graph lineage; one credential layer across the fleet). Kit adoption: the shared credential kit does not cover config.toml (a declared exemption, a credential source in Files), so credential-persisted-outside-the-store stays a hand-fix; the held-value funnel check was replaced by an explicit header filter (gradient's baseURLWithoutCredentials for base_url). TestConfigHeaderNeverKeepsTheNewKey (credwire) runs the built binary and was seen failing on the pre-kit tree (d814276a58, .review/seen/).

handfixes.summary: The api-key header and every API request go only to the scheme, host and port of the RESOLVED API base URL (https://<SALESBUILDR_TENANT>.salesbuildr.com/public-api, or SALESBUILDR_BASE_URL); every redirect hop must stay on that origin and a non-ASCII host never matches. SALESBUILDR_TENANT must be one DNS label and not the shipped placeholder your-tenant, else every request is refused (ErrTenantInvalid). Installed on every CLI, novel and MCP client by registerClientHook (internal/cli/salesbuildr_guard.go)
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning: the generated client sends the api-key header to whatever URL it is handed and splices {tenant} into the base URL as a raw string (internal/client/url.go buildURL), so a tenant such as `evil.example#` or `u@evil.example` moved the host and the key went with it. The pin is taken from the resolved URL (client.ResolvedBaseURL with the config's template vars); the guard ported from gradient url.Parse'd the {tenant} template, pinned nothing and refused every tenant request (seen/tenant-pin-seen-failing.log). The tenant refusal is cli.TenantPinnable, which credwire.showBaseURL also calls so the kit's allowed origin is the pinned host (credkit-wiring).

hc.Transport = originPinTripper{pin: pin, refusal: refusal, next: inner}

handfixes.summary: The hand-built read-only `sql` command (internal/cli/sql.go, SQLite mode=ro plus a keyword filter) is registered with a literal rootCmd.AddCommand in root.go
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 generates no `sql` command for this spec; the published novels (recipes, README `Catalog margin audit in SQL`, MCP intent catalog_margin_audit_in_sql) call it. root.go is generated, so a reprint drops the registration (tools/apply_edits.py re-applies it).

handfixes.summary: `sql` prints the --plain list (header line, one row per line) for an unformatted call under PRINTING_PRESS_VERIFY, and JSON everywhere else
handfixes.why: Root cause of the prior library copy's verify FAIL (32 domain tables, 0 rows after mock sync): verify's data-pipeline probe reads `sql` output as sqlite3 list mode, and the hand `sql` printed a JSON array on a pipe, so every count parsed as 0 although the store held the rows. Seen failing first (seen/sql-verify-format-seen-failing.log); verify-work-1.log Data Pipeline PASS 23 tables after.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err. The export is written once through credkit.WriteFile when complete.
handfixes.why: Carried from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint with the ported export.go edit: the generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` declared a new err, so the deferred close never ran after an API error and the unclosed filter pipe kept the process from exiting.

handfixes.summary: opportunity mrr-forecast reads probability as the documented 0-1 fraction (spec.json UpsertOpportunityDto.probability, minimum 0, maximum 1); an open deal outside that range is counted in probabilityOutOfRange and left out of the weighted totals
handfixes.why: Codex r1 (review) P1 class documented-fraction-read-as-percent: the forecast divided probability by 100, so a documented 0.5 on 1000 MRR weighed 5, not 500. Seen failing: seen/r1-documented-fraction-read-as-percent-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: Every novel reads numbers through one presence-aware parser (gnumOK): an explicit 0 quantity, markup or sales-cycle length is a value; only an absent field takes the fallback (one unit; markup from price over cost)
handfixes.why: Codex r1 (review) P1 class documented-zero-read-as-missing: QuoteItemResponseDto.quantity and .markup are required numbers (CreateQuoteProductDto allows quantity 0), but quantity 0 counted as one unit (quote funnel, stale, product velocity) and markup 0 as unknown (quote thin missed a zero-markup line); a 0-day sales cycle was left out of velocity. Seen failing: seen/r1-documented-zero-read-as-missing-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.why: Codex r1 (review) P1 class identifier-namespaces-merged: one pass matched id OR externalIdentifier OR name and returned the first row, so `company whitespace 1234` reported the company whose externalIdentifier is 1234 instead of the company whose id is 1234 (both documented CompanyResponseDto fields). handfixes.summary: A product or pricing-book entry with no price or cost is unknown, never 0: pricing drift compares only numbers both sides carry and counts the rest as incomparable; company whitespace prints a null price and sorts it last
handfixes.why: ProductResponseDto does not require price or cost, so a catalog product with no cost on file was reported as cost drift against 0 (bookCost 900 vs catalogCost 0, costDelta 900), and an unpriced product sorted and printed as price 0. Mirror case of review-r1-explicit-zero-is-a-value. Seen failing first: TestR2PricingDriftComparesOnlyNumbersBothSidesCarry, TestR2WhitespaceKeepsAnUnknownPriceUnknown.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO); ChatGPT on the web needs the operator's own HTTPS host with the MCP HTTP token (press 4.34.2 HTTP mode), and no page says HTTP mode is paused.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal (SecretEnv SALESBUILDR_API_KEY and SALESBUILDR_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN; Files = the config the run really uses first, an explicit --config or SALESBUILDR_CONFIG winning, then the 0600 credential store and the legacy config; every other config, store and profiles.json any --config or --home could mean is held with cliutil.HoldFile; ConfigFields and StoredRecords api_key, auth_header, access_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret; CredentialHeaders api-key and integration-key; CredentialFlags --integration-key; StdinFlags --stdin, a JSON body put on one line first and feedback's prose body handed back after Start (compactStdinBody, AfterStart); ResponseFields password, otp, pin, passcode and the integration key and api key names, matched exactly so useSignatureImage stays readable; BaseURL base_url, SALESBUILDR_BASE_URL, default https://{tenant}.salesbuildr.com/public-api; Origins base_url only, the MCP HTTP token allowed nowhere). The default is a template the kit cannot resolve, so credentialFiles calls showBaseURL, which resolves the tenant host the way the client does (config.Load, then client.ResolvedBaseURL; a tenant cli.TenantPinnable refuses shows nothing) and shows it to the kit through SALESBUILDR_BASE_URL; AfterStart, the statement after credkit.Start in both mains, puts the variable back. credkit.Exit ends both mains. Every sink is routed: stdout and stderr at the descriptor; the API client (client.OutboundGuard), feedback, deliver and the probe through credkit.Transport; cache, journal, teach log, profile, platform profile, rate-limit lock, export and delivery files through credkit.WriteFile, AppendFile and OpenFile; SQLite through internal/credsql (credkit-sqlite-every-handle); the MCP server through MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP (credkit-mcphttp-outermost); the MCP server's CLI child through RunCommand; terminal checks through credkit.Terminal; auth set-token holds the token it reads from stdin; the built auth header and a resolved client-profile credential are held where they are derived. The 0600 credential store and config.toml are credential sources: their writes are a declared exemption, outside the kit in cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile, and both are in Files.
handfixes.why: Retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, store-never-keeps-secrets, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld, startup-output-held-first, mcp-held-arguments-refused, undecoded-encodings-every-alignment, held-forms-in-every-encoding, response-credentials-held, every-text-encoding-withheld, outbound-split-parts-refused, auth-carrier-names-and-shapes-held, integration-key-held, review-r1-config-file-every-shape, review-r1-short-held-value-every-encoding, review-r1-numeric-credentials-held: replaced by the shared credential kit (entries removed: the ledger's retired list only takes retirements tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json backs). The connector's own holder, output chokepoint, secret funnel, encodings/outbound/short-value/secrets matchers, store withholding driver, config hold and MCP output wrappers grew per review round because each sink and encoding was closed one at a time; the kit is one shared implementation of the leak contract, checked byte for byte against tools/maintainer/credkit (vendor_credkit.py --check). The open Codex classes short-held-value-encoded and non-string-credential-not-held are closed by the kit: internal/credwire/open_classes_test.go TestShortHeldValueEncoded and TestNonStringCredentialNotHeld run the built binaries and were seen failing on the pre-kit tree (d814276a58, .review/seen/) and pass after. TestTenantHostIsTheAllowedOrigin proves the templated default resolves to the tenant host (seen failing with showBaseURL removed, .review/seen/tenant-origin-seen-failing.log). Kit notes, not hand-fixes: a short held value (under 8 characters) split across a space is not withheld; the kit's file stream withholds ordinary JSONL after about 20 KB, so export is buffered and written once.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal (a templated BaseURL default resolved for the kit) and the kit-wrapped SQLite driver.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name. The SALESBUILDR_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds is withheld by the shared credential kit at the sink (credkit-wiring). journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) returns the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, and records every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query. These are names the kit never holds, so they stay hand-fixes. Seen failing on the pre-kit tree (d814276a58, .review/seen/) and passing after; the shape and tests follow gradient's entry of the same id. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments.

handfixes.summary: credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains (credkit-wiring), so every credential in config.toml is held before the program can print a byte, a config that does not parse included. A credential in a malformed config.toml or in a base_url that does not parse never appears in salesbuildr-cli startup output (stdout and stderr) or in salesbuildr-mcp's stderr and JSON-RPC responses.
handfixes.why: Fleet rule (Startup ordering): the holder must be installed before config is loaded or any startup diagnostic can print, in both the CLI and the MCP server. internal/credwire/startup_test.go TestStartupConfigHeldFirst builds and runs both binaries (.exe on Windows) in a sandbox home. Proved both ways: with credkit.Start removed from both mains the base_url case fails (doctor prints a piece of the URL password; .review/seen/startup-config-held-first-seen-failing.log), and it passes with the kit (.review/mutant-restored-pass.log).

handfixes.summary: Every SQLite handle goes through credkit.SQLDriver: internal/credsql registers the one driver and every sql.Open in store.go and platform/migration.go names it, the read-only opener included. The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to a DSN parameter (credsql.LengthLimitParam, store.OpenReadOnlyValueCapped).
handfixes.why: A statement's text and bound values are a sink of their own, reads included. Replaces the connector's store withholding driver (store-never-keeps-secrets, removed under credkit-wiring).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate store, migration and MCP sql opens against one kit-wrapped driver name.

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing (Origin, bearer, bounded body read), then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the refusal it decided.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler, a refusal answers outside it, and a bearer holding the refusal's text would get a piece of itself back. Same shape as dropsuite's entry of the same id.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the kit-wrapped handler.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
